title: Port of Brisbane 99-year lease (Queensland)
summary: Queensland signed a 99-year lease of the Port of Brisbane to a private consortium on 10 November 2010.

instruments.title: Port of Brisbane lease transaction (authorising legislation not checked)

direction_rationale: Long-term leases move port monopolies to private owners: efficiency may improve, but so may the incentive to raise regulated or unregulated charges.

industries.name: Port and Water Transport Terminal Operations

comparison: Ports still in public hands (e.g. Fremantle); staggered lease dates 2010-2016

verified.notes: Date from a Queensland ministerial statement.

review.notes: Drafted by AI-assisted desk research on 18 October 2026 (legislation gap scan, docs/legislation_gap_scan.md) from the sources cited. Not yet checked by a person: verify dates, industries and the direction hypothesis before use.

assessment.summary: A long-term lease of a state-owned port to a private operator. Private owners may invest and run the port more efficiently, but a port is a local monopoly and lease terms can raise charges or deter rival ports.

marks.reason: Moves a port monopoly to a private owner under light-handed price regulation.
A private owner with a long lease has incentives to invest, and the proceeds funded other infrastructure.

responsible.note: Administers the Transport Infrastructure Act 1994, under which ports are managed; the lease itself was a Treasury transaction.
